display.purpose: Large stat-tile counts on the dashboard header - always mono because they're counts, not headlines.

headline.purpose: Drawer/modal titles - a company name, a new-table title.

title.purpose: Page header and modal section headers.

body.purpose: The default UI voice - buttons, labels, descriptions, list content.

label.purpose: Uppercase section eyebrows and muted metadata captions.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Marks a surface as floating above the page: the modal panel, the detail drawer, the login card. Never used on an at-rest card.

motion.name: hover-brightness
motion.purpose: The only hover treatment on filled buttons (primary/danger) - a brightness dip, never a color swap or scale transform.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one committing action per view (Sign in, + New Company, Amend Thesis).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #ccff00; color: #050505; padding: 6px 12px; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: filter 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ccff00; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The default for every non-primary action (Cancel, nav items, Post Observations).
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: transparent; color: #f0f0f0; padding: 6px 12px; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; border: 1px solid #333333; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #1a1a1a; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { background: #ff003c; color: #ffffff; padding: 6px 12px; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: filter 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { filter: brightness(0.9); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Nested-panel-toned form field with a lime focus glow.
components.css: .ds-input { background: #0a0a0a; color: #f0f0f0; border: 1px solid #333333; border-radius: 6px; padding: 6px 8px; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #888888; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #ccff00; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(204,255,0,0.25); }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: on_track/watch_closely/broken status indicator - 10% tint fill, full-strength text, thin same-color ring.
components.css: .ds-pill-good { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 2px 10px; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgba(204,255,0,0.1); color: #ccff00; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(204,255,0,0.2); font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Company card / stat tile - flat, hairline border, no shadow.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #121212; border: 1px solid #333333; border-radius: 8px; padding: 16px; } .ds-card-value { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 600; color: #f0f0f0; } .ds-card-label { font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #888888; margin-top: 4px; }

components.name: Data Table Row
components.description: The generic custom-table grid - mono numeric cells, pill-badge enum cells, no zebra striping.
components.css: .ds-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-table thead tr { background: #0a0a0a; } .ds-table th { text-align: left; padding: 8px 12px; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #888888; } .ds-table td { padding: 8px 12px; border-top: 1px solid #333333; color: #f0f0f0; } .ds-table-num { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; } .ds-table-badge { display: inline-block; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #1a1a1a; font-size: 0.75rem; }

narrative.overview:
This is instrumentation for a decision that costs real money if it's wrong. The console metaphor comes from the product's own defining mechanism, kill triggers: pre-committed, quantified conditions that invalidate a thesis before the analyst gets emotionally invested in being right. The interface should feel like it belongs to that discipline - built for someone who has already decided that clarity beats comfort.

But the execution stays quiet, not loud. This is not a garish trading-floor wall of blinking tickers. It's near-black and mostly silent, with exactly one accent color (Signal Lime) reserved for the things that actually matter: primary commit actions, on-track status, the thing you must not miss. Everything else recedes into graphite and grey so that when color appears, it means something. Numbers and keys render in a distinct monospaced voice, because in this product a number is evidence, not decoration - it should look like it came from an instrument, not from prose.

The palette and every accent are shared, unchanged, between a near-black default theme and a white-ground light theme, only the ground and text tokens swap. A screen that only works in one theme is a bug, not a variant.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground by default, white-ground light theme with the exact same accents - never redesign per theme, only re-ground it.

One accent (Signal Lime) carries primary action and 'good' status; three siblings (Cyan, Red, Amber) are reserved for secondary/info, danger, and warning respectively - never freelanced for decoration.
Flat at rest; shadow is reserved for things that float above the page.
Numbers, keys, and code are always monospaced (JetBrains Mono), regardless of size - prose is always Space Grotesk.
Refined and quiet in execution: rectangular controls, no gradients, generous quiet space, restraint over spectacle.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Lime is the only color that ever means "primary action" or "this is good." If a screen has more than one lime element competing for attention, something is wrong - dilute to Cyan, Amber, or plain Graphite instead of adding a second hero color.

rules.name: The Dark-Ink Pairing Rule
rules.body: Text on any bright accent fill (Lime, Cyan, Amber) is Void Black, never white. Kill Red is the sole exception, used for the one truly urgent, alarm-toned action.

rules.name: The Data Voice Rule
rules.body: Any number, key, code snippet, or machine-shaped value renders in JetBrains Mono, at whatever size the context calls for. Any word a human composed renders in Space Grotesk. Never mix the two within a single value.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: No card, tile, badge, or button carries a shadow at rest or on hover. Shadow exists solely to mark a surface as floating above the page (modal, drawer, login card).

dos: Do keep Signal Lime to primary actions and 'good' status only - it is a signal, not a brand wash.
Do render every number, key, and code value in JetBrains Mono regardless of its size or context.
Do use Void Black text on bright accent fills (Lime, Cyan, Amber); reserve white text for Kill Red only.
Do keep cards and panels flat with a hairline border; reserve shadow-xl for modals, the drawer, and the login card only.
Do carry the same four accent hues, unchanged, across both the dark and light theme - only ground and text tokens may swap.
donts: Don't add a second 'hero' accent color competing with Signal Lime on the same screen.
Don't use rounded-full or soft pill shapes on buttons or cards - full rounding is reserved for status dots, pills, and badges.
Don't add a shadow to an at-rest card, tile, or button; shadow means 'floating above the page,' nothing else.
Don't mix Space Grotesk into a data value or JetBrains Mono into prose - the two fonts are a semantic split, not a stylistic one.
Don't introduce a second border color; Hairline Grey (or its light-theme counterpart) is the only one.
